prerequisites: Positive completion of the StEOP (StudienEingangs- und OrientierungsPhase - study entry and orientation phase)

learning_outcomes.text: Students can apply mass, momentum, and energy balances to fluid mechanics and heat transfer problems and derive the governing equations. They can analyze and calculate heat transfer processes due to conduction, forced and natural convection, as well as radiation, and also processes with phase transitions.
Define terms such as temperature, heat, internal energy, phase, heat flux density.
Apply control volumes to flow and temperature fields, choose the correct boundary conditions, and derive the basic equations from them.
Assess whether dissipation needs to be considered in the description of processes.
Completely calculate simple laminar shear flows, deduce characteristic parameters from them, and apply these to similar problems.
Distinguish between natural and forced convection.
Explain differences in flow and heat transfer around slender and blunt bodies.
Recognize chimney flow, buoyant jets, and boundary layers, apply the Boussinesq approximation to them, and calculate heat transfer.
Distinguish between laminar and turbulent flows, explain their major differences, and determine heat transfer in turbulent boundary layers and turbulent pipe flow.
Distinguish the different instability mechanisms in Rayleigh-Bénard convection.
Consider melting or vaporization enthalpy during phase transitions and thus calculate one-dimensional solidification processes or Nusselt's water film.
Describe and calculate radiation fields and radiation exchange using radiation intensity, absorption and emission capabilities, and their spectral properties.
Assess the possibility of physical processes based on their entropy balance.
Explain derivations, assumptions, and boundary conditions in a comprehensible manner.
Present results appropriately for the audience and using correct technical language.

syllabus_topics: Coupling of electrical current – heat flow
Laminar, turbulent, and compressible boundary layers
Heat transfer on slender and blunt bodies
Boundary layer on the vertical wall
assessment_rules: The lecture-exercise is assessed through written tests. Specific examination modalities are communicated via the information system before the start of each semester.
